metaTitle: Azure ADLS: The Definitive Guide for Data Lakehouse
metaDescription: Learn what Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 is, how it serves as the object storage foundation for Azure-based Apache Iceberg lakehouses, and its key features for enterprise data.
h1: Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS): The Definitive Guide
lede: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (ADLS Gen2) is Microsoft's enterprise-grade object storage for data lakehouses on Azure. Its hierarchical namespace, Azure AD integration, and ACL-based access control make it the natural storage layer for Apache Iceberg tables on Microsoft Azure.

faqs.a: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 is Microsoft's cloud object storage service optimized for big data analytics. It combines Azure Blob Storage's unlimited scale and low cost with a hierarchical namespace and POSIX-compatible ACLs for fine-grained access control. It is the recommended storage backend for Apache Iceberg lakehouses on Microsoft Azure.

faqs.q: How does ADLS Gen2 differ from Azure Blob Storage?
faqs.a: ADLS Gen2 is built on Azure Blob Storage but adds a hierarchical namespace (true directory semantics with atomic rename), POSIX ACLs (file and directory level permissions), and optimized drivers for big data workloads (ABFS protocol). Standard Blob Storage uses a flat namespace and only container-level RBAC.

faqs.q: Does Apache Iceberg support ADLS Gen2?
faqs.a: Yes. Apache Iceberg, Dremio, Spark, and Trino all support ADLS Gen2 as a storage backend via the Azure Blob File System (ABFS) driver. Iceberg stores data files and metadata in ADLS Gen2 containers using the abfss:// URI scheme.

sections.heading: What Is Azure ADLS Gen2?
sections.content:
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (ADLS Gen2) is Microsoft's enterprise object storage service for data lakes and lakehouses on Azure. It combines Azure Blob Storage's unlimited scale and cost efficiency with a hierarchical namespace (enabling true directory semantics and atomic directory operations) and POSIX ACLs (file and directory-level permissions compatible with Hadoop security models).

For Apache Iceberg lakehouses on Azure, ADLS Gen2 is the recommended storage backend. Iceberg data files (Parquet) and metadata files (Avro manifests, JSON table metadata) are stored as ADLS Gen2 blobs in containers, accessed via the ABFS (Azure Blob File System) protocol using the abfss:// URI scheme.

sections.heading: ADLS and Dremio Cloud on Azure
sections.content: Dremio Cloud on Azure uses ADLS Gen2 as the BYOS (Bring Your Own Storage) backend. Organizations connect their own ADLS Gen2 containers to Dremio Cloud, and Dremio's managed execution engines read and write Iceberg tables in those containers. Azure AD service principals and managed identities handle authentication, with Dremio's Open Catalog providing credential vending for per-table scoped access.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.content: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 is the storage foundation for Azure-based data lakehouses. Its hierarchical namespace, Azure AD integration, and POSIX ACLs make it enterprise-ready for governed Apache Iceberg deployments. For organizations standardizing on Microsoft Azure, ADLS Gen2 provides the same decoupled storage-and-compute benefits as Amazon S3 with Azure-native identity and security integration.
